title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, carried over from the previous page. Start with two morphisms of topoi α, β: X' ⇉ X. The category 𝓛(α,β) (also written 𝒢) has as objects the pairs (E, F_E), where E is a sheaf on X and F_E: α*(E) → β*(E) is a morphism. On the previous page this was shown, modulo checking, to be a topos via Giraud's criterion and SGA4 I 9.21–9.25. The forgetful functor (E, F_E) ↦ E is the inverse image of a morphism of topoi ω_X: X → 𝓛(α,β). The pair (ω_X, the canonical 2-cell between ω_X∘α and ω_X∘β) is characterised by a universal property ('l'axiome de la caractérisation universelle de la paire'). In modern 2-categorical language, 𝓛(α,β) is the lax coequaliser (coinserter) of α and β in the 2-category of topoi. Dually, on inverse images, its category of sheaves is the inserter of α* and β*. The motivating special case is X' = X, β = id, α = f_X a Frobenius. The objects are then sheaves with a Frobenius structure f_X*E → E, i.e. F-modules / F-crystal-type objects. This is the relevance to the folder 'Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham'.

This page, step 1 (functoriality). Take a square, commutative up to isomorphism, between the pairs (α,β): X' ⇉ X and (λ,μ): Y' ⇉ Y, with u_1: X' → Y' and u_0: X → Y. The universal property gives a morphism of topoi v = 𝓛(u): 𝓛(α,β) → 𝓛(λ,μ), with transitivity isomorphisms, and with ω_Y ∘ u_0 ≅ v ∘ ω_X. Grothendieck crossed out 'foncteur' and replaced it with 'morphisme de topos'.

Step 2 (explicit description). He notes that v_* and v^* can be made explicit as in his n°1, by specialising to X' = X, Y' = Y, β = id, μ = id, α = f_X, λ = f_Y. This is the Frobenius case, with u_0 compatible with the Frobenii.

Step 3 (base change for higher direct images). For an abelian object E = (E, F_E) of 𝓛(α,β), there are base-change maps from the underlying sheaf of R^i v_*(E) to R^i u_{0*}(E). Here ω_X^*(E) = E is the underlying sheaf on X. One wants these to be isomorphisms, i.e. computing higher direct images commutes with forgetting the Frobenius structure. Only i = 0 is clear. The standard strategy is to show that if E is an injective abelian object of 𝓛(α,β), then its underlying sheaf E is acyclic in the sense of SGA4 V (flasque). Grothendieck says it suffices that α* and β* commute with infinite products, i.e. that α_! and β_! exist (α, β essential morphisms). The next page adds that then ω_X is also essential, i.e. ω_{X!} exists. The free-object construction makes this plausible: in the case β = id the free object on G is ⊕_n (α*)^n G, and in general one needs β_!.
errors: Source mismatch in the base-change map as written. Grothendieck writes ω_X^*(R^i v_*(E)) → R^i u_{0*}(E), but R^i v_*(E) lives on 𝓛(λ,μ). Its underlying sheaf on Y is ω_Y^*(R^i v_*E), so the map should read ω_Y^*(R^i v_* E) → R^i u_{0*}(ω_X^* E). This is a slip of index (ω_X for ω_Y); the image does seem to show ω_X.

Gap in the sufficiency claim. Existence of ω_{X!} (ω_X essential) does not by itself make ω_X^* send injectives to injectives; that would need the abelian left adjoint to be exact. What is needed is only that ω_X^* sends injectives to flasque sheaves, and this requires an argument along SGA4 V lines that is not given. The margin note 'à vérifier' on the previous page signals the same provisional status.

'Commutent aux produits finis' in the machine transcription cannot be right: inverse images always commute with finite products. The intended condition is commutation with arbitrary (infinite) products, equivalent to the existence of α_! and β_!.

ideas.what: Topos 𝓛(α,β) of pairs (E, α*E → β*E) attached to two morphisms of topoi, with a universal property ('caractérisation universelle de la paire') and functoriality in the pair.
ideas.modern_name: Lax coequaliser / coinserter in the 2-category of topoi (inserter of α*, β*); in the Frobenius case, the category of F-sheaves / sheaves with Frobenius structure (a lax 'mapping torus').
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lax colimits of topoi: categorical topos theory of the 1970s–80s (e.g. Makkai–Paré, Moerdijk); F-sheaf categories: Deligne (SGA 4½, 'Fonctions L modulo ℓ^n et modulo p'), Katz, later Böckle–Pink and Emerton–Kisin.
ideas.where_published: SGA4 VI treats fibred topoi and lax limits in related form; a topos of Frobenius pairs as a coinserter is not known to me in SGA.

ideas.what: Morphism of topoi 𝓛(u) induced by a square of pairs, compatible with ω_X and ω_Y.
Base change R^i v_* versus R^i u_{0*} under the forgetful functor, reduced to showing injectives of 𝓛 have acyclic underlying sheaves when α, β are essential.
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of derived pushforward with forgetting the Frobenius structure (cohomology of F-modules / F-crystals computed on the underlying sheaves).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Deligne SGA 4½ and Böckle–Pink's theory of crystals over function fields.

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a general topos-theoretic framework for Frobenius-structured sheaves: the coinserter topos of a pair α, β of topos morphisms, with functoriality and a base-change problem for R^i v_*. He leaves the acyclicity of injectives under the essentiality hypothesis to be checked.
missed.quote: on aimerait savoir que ce sont des isom., seulement que c'est le cas pour i=0. On obligé pratiquement d'établir que si E est un faisceau abélien injectif de 𝓛(α,β), alors E est un faisceau acyclique
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: F-sheaves and F-crystals are usually handled as abelian categories of modules with an extra map, not as topoi. Grothendieck's viewpoint, a lax coequaliser topos in which F-objects are genuine sheaves on a topos, is closer to modern work. Examples are Weil-étale topoi and 'Frobenius fixed point' constructions such as Scholze–Clausen's lax-equaliser / 'mapping torus' formalism for φ-modules. This 1960s precursor seems unrecorded, though the result itself is fairly standard.

deep.surprise_reason: An early, explicit use of the lax coequaliser (coinserter) of topoi to house Frobenius-structured sheaves, with a universal property and a base-change problem. The ingredients are individually standard, but this topos-theoretic packaging of F-sheaves by Grothendieck in the crystalline context is not, as far as I know, in the record.
transcription_corrections: The topos is written 𝓛(α,β) here but 𝒢(α,β) on the previous page; it is the same object.
'alors E est un faisceau acyclique [-E-]' corresponds to 'acyclique (SGA4 V)': a crossed-out letter followed by the reference.
'commutent aux produits finis [?] (i.e. α_!, β_! exacts)' should probably read 'commutent aux produits infinis (i.e. α_!, β_! existent)', consistent with the next page's 'i.e. ω_{X!} existe'.
'à isom. non [?] près' should probably read 'à isom. près' (the second phrase likely reads 'à isom. canon. près').
'seulement [?] que c'est le cas pour i=0' should probably read 'on sait seulement que c'est le cas pour i=0'.
'on a des "hom. de chgt. de base"' is correct; the faint word under it is 'dans' ('des "hom. de chgt. de base" dans...').
